morphology.capsule: Some strains have a thin polysaccharide microcapsule

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human skin and anterior nares (nasal mucosa)
habitat.hostAssociation: Commensal in roughly a third of healthy adults via nasal carriage; opportunistic pathogen
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Can survive on dry surfaces for extended periods
habitat.reservoir: Human nares and skin; hospital environment for MRSA strains

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe, halotolerant — grows in high-salt media that inhibits most other organisms

identificationClues: Catalase positive — distinguishes it from Streptococcus
Coagulase positive — distinguishes it from coagulase-negative staphylococci
Ferments mannitol on MSA (yellow color change)

diseases: Skin and soft tissue infections (abscesses, cellulitis, impetigo)
virulenceFactors: Protein A — binds the Fc region of antibodies, antiphagocytic
toxins: Enterotoxins — cause of staphylococcal food poisoning
clinicalImportance.transmission: Direct contact, fomites, and autoinoculation from nasal carriage
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections; MRSA is a major driver of both hospital- and community-acquired disease
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: The coagulase test is the key differentiator from other, generally less virulent staphylococci

examFacts.importantDisease: Skin/soft tissue infections; toxic shock syndrome
examFacts.importantTest: Coagulase test — differentiates from coagulase-negative staph
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Coagulase-positive, golden-pigmented colonies that ferment mannitol
